title: Classical guitar close view, 18 s excerpt (archive.org, CC0 1.0)
what: Real classical guitar video (nylon strings; a Yamaha C-40 per the item description), played with the fingers, 18 s excerpt (200-218 s) of a 580.5 s home recording; 1920x1080, 25 fps, progressive. The picture fills the left 1438x1080 of the frame; the right 482 columns are black, as in the source. One fixed camera facing the player and the guitar top at about chest height; no cut inside the excerpt (the only cut in the whole video, ffmpeg scene score > 0.12, is at 287.08 s, where a second take starts). Close view: the player's face is out of frame; the neck runs diagonally to the upper right, with the nut and part of the headstock at the upper-right edge, and the whole fretboard from the nut to the sound hole is in frame (on the frame at 209 s of the original: the nut, fret 1 and 14 more fret wires, frets 5 to 18 by their spacing, with frets 2-4 under the fingers). The fretting hand (left) is on the neck and fully in frame, in the low positions in the frames looked at (one every 3 s); the picking-hand fingers (right) are at the sound hole at the left edge of the picture, partly cut off by it. No capo. Audio: both channels carry the same signal (left minus right is -117.7 dBFS RMS in R3b.wav), i.e. a mono recording stored as stereo; R3b.wav peaks at -13.1 dBFS. The piece played is not identified in the item's metadata. No ground truth.
